title.en: Raw data and why we classify

body.en: Data collected in their original, unorganised form are called *raw data*. Classification is the process of arranging raw data into groups or classes according to common characteristics. It makes data concise, easy to compare and ready for analysis.
body.kn: ಮೂಲ ರೂಪದ ಅಸಂಘಟಿತ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವೇ ಕಚ್ಚಾ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ. ಸಮಾನ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಗುಂಪುಗಳಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುವುದು ವರ್ಗೀಕರಣ.

title.en: Classify raw marks into a frequency table

narration.en: Twenty students' marks (out of 100) are raw data: hard to read. Grouping them into classes of equal width (0–10, 10–20 …, each including its lower limit) gives a frequency table. Wider classes are simpler but hide detail. Use width 10. Which class has the most students? Switch to width 25. Do the frequencies still add up to 20?
narration.kn: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳ ಅಂಕಗಳು (100ಕ್ಕೆ) ಕಚ್ಚಾ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ: ಓದಲು ಕಷ್ಟ. ಸಮಾನ ಅಗಲದ ವರ್ಗಗಳಾಗಿ (0–10, 10–20 …, ಕೆಳಮಿತಿ ಸೇರಿ) ಗುಂಪು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ. ಅಗಲ ವರ್ಗ ಸರಳ, ಆದರೆ ವಿವರ ಮರೆಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಅಗಲ 10 ಬಳಸಿ. ಯಾವ ವರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು? ಅಗಲ 25ಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಿಸಿ. ಆವೃತ್ತಿಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ ಇನ್ನೂ 20 ಆಗಿದೆಯೇ?

title.en: On the board: Four ways to classify

say.en: Raw data arrive as a jumble of figures. Classification puts them into groups with a common feature.
By time is chronological. By place is spatial.
By an attribute is qualitative. By a measured value is quantitative.
Classified data are concise, easy to compare and ready for analysis.
On the board: Four ways to classify.

Wheat output of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh

explanation.en: Chronological classification is by time, spatial by place, qualitative by an attribute that cannot be measured, and quantitative by a measurable characteristic.

body.en: Chronological *classification* groups data by time (years, months). Spatial classification groups data by place (states, districts). Qualitative classification groups by attributes such as gender or literacy. Quantitative classification groups by measurable characteristics such as marks, income or height.
body.kn: ಕಾಲಾನುಕ್ರಮ (ಸಮಯದ ಆಧಾರ), ಪ್ರಾದೇಶಿಕ (ಸ್ಥಳದ ಆಧಾರ), ಗುಣಾತ್ಮಕ (ಗುಣಗಳ ಆಧಾರ) ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಮಾಣಾತ್ಮಕ (ಅಳತೆಯ ಆಧಾರ) ವರ್ಗೀಕರಣ.

problem.en: Name the type of classification: (a) rice output of Karnataka, Punjab and West Bengal; (b) India's exports in 2020, 2021, 2022; (c) employees by marital status; (d) workers grouped by daily wage ₹300–400, ₹400–500.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Name the type of classification: (a) rice output of Karnataka, Punjab and West Bengal; (b) India's exports in 2020, 2021, 2022; (c) employees by marital status; (d) workers grouped by daily wage ₹300–400, ₹400–500.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Name the type of classification: a rice output of Karnataka, Punjab and West Bengal; b India's exports in 2020, 2021, 2022; c employees by marital status; d workers grouped by daily wage 300 rupees-400, 400 rupees-500.
a By place: spatial.
b By year: chronological.
c By attribute: qualitative.
d By a measured value: quantitative.
So the answer is a spatial, b chronological, c qualitative, d quantitative.

body.en: Ask "By what are we grouping?" Time → chronological, Place → spatial, Attribute → qualitative, Measure → quantitative.
